headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to bear more of the costs for new grid infrastructure they necessitate, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Governor Spanberger's administration, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia moves to shift more power costs from families to data centers
news_summary: Virginia regulators are re-evaluating how to allocate the costs of transmission infrastructure, with a new order potentially shifting a larger share of these expenses to data centers and other major power users. This decision, supported by Governor Spanberger's administration, aims to protect households and small businesses from bearing the costs of grid upgrades driven by data center growth.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates that water users providing water to data centers report their total water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for public transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency on water consumption by the rapidly growing data center industry, addressing concerns about dwindling groundwater supplies.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulation
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high-energy-use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Thomas.
news_headline: Data centers defined as "high-energy-use" may need noise and energy-provider disclosure
news_summary: Under HB153/SB94, facilities requiring 100 megawatts or more, primarily data centers, will trigger special-exception submission requirements. This includes a mandatory noise study for schools and residences within 500 feet and a statement from the energy provider on anticipated demand and source.
